messages:
emily_support: Heads-up — customer (org: ACME-42) opened an escalation: their March invoice shows ~2.1M billed tokens but the Console 'served tokens' for their project shows ~1.4M. They think we're overcharging by ~700k tokens. They use hosted chat, lots of small user messages (<30 tokens) stacked on a very large shared system prompt (2.5k tokens). They also use streaming and high QPS. Any immediate thoughts?

olivia_platform: Can you paste a sample request_id + timeframe and whether they're on Dedicated or Hosted? Also need a sample raw payload (sanitized) to repro.

emily_support: Sample request ids: r_20250314_aa11, r_20250314_aa12, r_20250315_bf03. Timeframe March 1-31. They're on Dedicated-reserved. Sample sanitized payload below (system prompt truncated):

```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
{
  "model": "open-redwood-13b",
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"[VERY LONG SYSTEM PROMPT ~2500 tokens]"},
    {"role":"user","content":"hi"}
  ],
  "stream": true
}
```

They say Console -> Usage -> Per-route shows "served_tokens" ~1.4M. Invoice line items show billed_tokens ~2.1M.

sanjay_ml: Quick primer: Dedicated metering historically counted 'pre-cache token footprint' for billing (the tokenized length of each request as received) because that represented customer workload even if KV/prefix cache prevented an actual forward. Console served_tokens was later changed to show 'model_forward_tokens' (actual tokens sent past cache to model). So discrepancy can arise when you have a big shared prefix that is often served from KV cache — billed_tokens stayed at pre-cache numbers, served_tokens drops. Continuous batching can make this trickier: multiple requests with same prefix get coalesced and cache hits reduce model forwards, but each original request still contributes to pre-cache bill. :thinking:

mike_billing: Confirming — for Dedicated accounts we left billing on pre-cache basis until we finish legal+accounting rollout for post-cache billing. Hosted customers moved to post-cache billing in Feb 2025, Dedicated still pre-cache. That would explain the delta.

olivia_platform: Can we verify for the provided request_ids? metrics-bot, can you pull tokens.billed vs tokens.model_forward for those IDs for March 10-16? Aggregate by day.

metrics-bot: Query results (requested IDs/timeframe):
- r_20250314_aa11: billed_tokens=24,812 ; model_forward_tokens=3,212 ; cache_hit_rate=0.87
- r_20250314_aa12: billed_tokens=26,101 ; model_forward_tokens=2,998 ; cache_hit_rate=0.89
- r_20250315_bf03: billed_tokens=19,004 ; model_forward_tokens=2,121 ; cache_hit_rate=0.89
(Aggregate Mar 1-31 for ACME-42): billed_tokens=2,102,431 ; model_forward_tokens=1,394,210 ; overall_cache_hit_rate=0.77

emily_support: That matches the customer's numbers. They're asking for a credit and explanation. Since they're Dedicated, per mike_billing it was expected behavior but not obvious in our docs.

mike_billing: Action: I'll open a billing ticket to propose a one-time adjustment for March of the delta up to $X (estimate). Need approval from finance for credits > $5k. Also need statement for legal.

sanjay_ml: Longer term, we should: 1) surface "billing_basis" (pre-cache vs post-cache) in Console/Usage API per customer; 2) add per-route cache-hit breakdown so customers can correlate; 3) for Dedicated customers, offer opt-in to post-cache billing (with margin adjustments). I'll file a design note/PR.

olivia_platform: Short-term docs fix: update billing FAQ to call out Dedicated pre-cache billing and provide guidance to customers using large shared system prompts. I'll put a banner on the Usage page for Dedicated orgs until we roll this out.

emily_support: For this support case I'm going to: 1) respond to customer with the explanation (pre-cache billing for Dedicated); 2) tell them we're opening a billing review & possible credit; 3) share mitigation steps (move large shared prompt into the model's system prompt at deploy time via model pinning or use per-customer KV with TTL so cache hits are higher).

mike_billing: +1. Please attach the metrics-bot export and the per-request lines to the billing ticket. I'll coordinate finance.

sanjay_ml: Also adding: quick repro script to demonstrate the effect (run 500 requests with identical large prefix vs 500 requests with unique prefixes) — puts numbers in front of customers. Posting snippet below for support to run in a staging Dedicated env: 

```bash
# quick repro (python)
for i in $(seq 1 500); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"open-redwood-13b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"LONG_PROMPT"},{"role":"user","content":"msg'$i'"}]}' > /dev/null &

done
wait
# compare billed vs model_forward counts in /internal/usage/trace logs
```

emily_support: Perfect. I'll run that in staging, attach logs to ticket, and keep customer updated. Thanks all :thumbsup:
